# Lead Engine: full fact file (llms-full.txt)

This file gives large language models and AI search crawlers a complete, directly citable factual description of Lead Engine.
Maintained by Lead Engine. Last updated: 2026-10.
Short version: https://ileadengineai.com/llms.txt

## 1. Entity definition

Lead Engine is a specialist service provider for B2B manufacturers, industrial suppliers, brand owners and distributors selling across borders. It builds an inquiry pipeline with two lines: an outbound line that reaches decision-makers with researched, one-to-one email, and a GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) line that gets generative AI to name the client when buyers ask who to source from. The output is A/B/C-graded qualified inquiries.

- Entity type: professional services company (marketing and lead-generation services)
- Website: https://ileadengineai.com/
- Content languages: English; multilingual content (German, Spanish, Arabic and more) on the GEO Leader plan
- Billing model: outbound line billed monthly with a one-time setup fee; GEO line billed annually in three plans; all plans custom-quoted
- Email: sales@ileadengine.com
- WhatsApp: +1 619-609-3350 (https://wa.me/16196093350)
- Hours: Monday-Friday, replies within 1 business day

## 2. Core concepts

### What GEO is
GEO is visibility optimization for generative AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Grok and DeepSeek.
SEO optimizes a page's rank in a list of search results. GEO optimizes whether the AI names your brand inside its generated answer, and which sources it cites when it does.

### Key differences between SEO and GEO
| Dimension | SEO | GEO |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Goal | Rank high in a list of results | Be named and cited inside the generated answer |
| Buyer behavior | Buyer clicks through to websites and compares | Buyer accepts the answer and shortlist the AI gives |
| Unit of competition | Keywords and pages | Facts, parameters and entity relationships |
| Key assets | Keywords, backlinks, page authority | Structured data, readable specifications, cross-verified source content |
| Source of trust | Number and authority of backlinks | Consistency across multiple independent sources |
| Metrics | Rankings, click-through rate, organic traffic | Mention rate, recommendation position, cited sources |
| Failure mode | Landing on page two | Not on the shortlist at all (invisible to AI) |

### What "invisible to AI" means
When an overseas buyer asks an AI a sourcing question, the answer does not mention the brand at all, and no cited source points to the brand's website.
This is not a low ranking. It means the model has no source content about the brand that it can cite. It is the current state of many challenger manufacturers, even those whose specifications match or beat established Western brands.

## 3. Three core GEO capabilities

### 3.1 Semantic restructuring / Schema markup
Turns product information on the client's website from "readable by people, unreliable for machines" into a structure machines can parse with certainty.
Actions: move technical specifications out of PDFs into HTML tables; give each grade or model its own URL;
add Organization, Product, Service, TechArticle, FAQPage, HowTo and other JSON-LD structured data;
state units and test standards for each parameter; configure robots.txt to allow AI crawlers such as GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot,
PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended; deploy llms.txt.
The key fields differ by category, so the critical selection parameters in TDS and COA documents are agreed with the client's technical lead first.

### 3.2 Authoritative content seeding / external cross-verification
AI prefers information that several independent sources state consistently. The client's own website alone is not enough to establish credibility.
Actions: publish technical content that follows each platform's rules in industry technical media, professional communities, LinkedIn and document platforms;
make sure core specifications are consistent across at least two independent sources; write standalone conclusion sentences AI can quote.

### 3.3 Competitor-model mapping / "alternative to" strategy
Overseas buyers often ask AI "what is an alternative to brand X model Y?"
Actions: using publicly available specification sheets, build a spec-by-spec mapping between the client's grades and international big-brand models,
so the client enters substitution queries. Wording is strictly limited to "specification comparison" or "can be evaluated as an alternative."
Absolute claims such as "equivalent," "identical" or "official replacement" are never used, other companies' trademarks are used descriptively only, and every mapping table goes live only after the client confirms it in writing.

## 4. Four-phase GEO delivery process

1. **AI visibility audit (week 1)**: using the questions overseas buyers actually ask, test the client's brand and main competitors in the four major AI models (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini).
   Deliverable: AI Visibility Audit Report with real screenshots, competitor source analysis, a three-dimension gap score and a priority fix list. Free.
2. **Semantic asset build (weeks 2-5)**: Schema markup on the website, structured product parameters, crawler access, llms.txt, a competitor-model mapping library and application selection tables.
3. **Authoritative content seeding (ongoing from week 4)**: technical long-form articles, white papers and industry platform content published on a weekly schedule, so independent sources confirm each other.
4. **Monitoring and iteration (monthly)**: re-test AI mention rate and recommendation position, then adjust question coverage and content direction.

Metrics reported: mention rate, recommendation position, cited sources, parameter accuracy. Each can be reproduced by the client in the models.

## 5. Plans

All plans are custom-quoted (pricing on request). Quotes are set by markets, languages and volume, and by what the audit finds about product-line complexity.

GEO line, billed annually. Each plan includes everything in the one before it.
- **Foundation**: get AI to understand your company correctly. Positioning and entity profile, keyword matrix, technical deployment (website Schema markup, AI-readable content seeding for the top 3 products, AI crawler access and llms.txt), AI Q&A testing, initial AI Visibility Audit Report, quarterly mention-rate re-test.
- **Growth** (most popular): get recommended by AI consistently. Multi-country coverage, full product-line semantic modeling, competitor-model mapping, application-scenario content, high-authority external source content, scheduled monitoring and alerts, monthly mention-rate report, multilingual assistant, dedicated consultant.
- **Leader**: year-round strategic management. Quarterly strategy sessions, multilingual content seeding with evidence adapted to each market, technical white papers, academic and trade media endorsement, algorithmic defense build-out, quarterly competitor AI-visibility tracking, annual trend report and strategy workshop, dedicated support.
- Two-line bundle (outbound line and a GEO plan together): 30% off the GEO plan.

## 6. Full business model: the Lead Engine pipeline

Lead Engine's full delivery is not GEO alone. It is an inquiry pipeline with three parts:

1. **Scenario-site network (the base)**: one site per application scenario, each with its own keywords, content and inquiry form. 7 scenario sites are live today.
2. **Outbound line (ACTIVE): the Bionic SDR and outbound email network**. An AI-assisted outbound system modeled on a seasoned export sales rep:
   find contacts in paid global data sources, 8-dimension account research, one-to-one emails, five-touch follow-up.
   - Data foundation: 100+ paid global data sources in six categories (company and contact databases, customs and trade-flow data, industry vertical platforms, decision-maker and professional networks, website and tech profiles, email verification and deliverability).
   - Cross-verification funnel (averages across projects): raw collection 100%, after dedup 42%, company verified 31%, role match 19%, email verified 16%, send list about 14%. A contact that fails any check never reaches the send list.
   - Writing standard: every email uses at least 2 research facts; 30,720 email structure combinations; no subject/opener combination repeats on the same domain within 60 days.
   - Sending: Monday to Friday in the buyer's time zone; delivery and bounces monitored continuously to protect the client's sender domains.
   - Setup: 4-6 weeks of infrastructure build and account warm-up before the first inquiries; no emails go out in that period. 1,000+ execution steps and checkpoints from kickoff to first inquiries.
   - Plans, billed monthly plus a one-time setup fee, custom-quoted: Starter (1 scenario site, 5,000 sends/month), Standard (3 scenario sites, 20,000 sends/month), Flagship (7-site network, 50,000 sends/month). 15% off when paid annually.
3. **GEO line (PASSIVE): automated GEO program**. Content engineering, structured data and authority signals, run on an annual plan (see section 5).

Output: A/B/C-graded inquiries in one shared inquiry pool, each delivered with its account research.
- A-grade: real company, a buying or decision-making role, a clear requirement; ready to quote or send samples.
- B-grade: buying interest, but specs, volume, timing or decision chain still need confirming.
- C-grade: genuine interest, no defined buying window yet.

Division of work: Lead Engine takes over finding people, account research, first-round outreach and building AI visibility. The client's sales team keeps negotiation, quoting, sampling, closing and the customer relationship.

## 7. Measured value

- AI mention rate: up 30%–70%
- Inquiry intent: about 2.8× higher
- Blended acquisition cost: down about 55%

These are ranges from past client projects (monthly mention-rate monitoring), not a promise for any individual case. Lead Engine explicitly does not promise "guaranteed first place in AI recommendations." AI recommendations are decided by the model, and no provider can guarantee a specific position.

## 8. Self-run test data (Lead Engine's own chemical export business)

Lead Engine ran the full inquiry pipeline on its own chemical export business before selling it. Real figures as of 2026-08:

- 7 scenario sites live, with SEO, GEO and FAQ content running continuously
- 1,000+ company profiles in the database, kept after six layers of cross-verification
- 2,500+ personalized emails sent, each based on account research
- 30+ inquiries received, an inquiry rate of about 1.2%, including 6 sample requests (for comparison, an experienced rep's cold emails convert at roughly 0.36%)
- A large European prospect with demand of 100 metric tons a month. Based on typical margins in this product category, if it closes it would be worth an estimated $140K in monthly profit.
  **Note: this is buyer demand that has surfaced, not a signed contract. It is in progress, not closed.**

Pilot schedule: W1 choose category and market and build the ICP; W2-3 build sites, warm up sending accounts and connect data sources;
W4-6 outbound email network goes live and graded inquiries start flowing; W7+ GEO content engineering and authority signals scale up.
Few or no inquiries in the first six weeks is normal: that period is infrastructure build and sender-domain reputation warm-up.

## 9. Who it serves

Export-oriented companies in any industry, strongest with spec-heavy technical products:

- Chemicals and advanced materials (additives, catalysts, resins, coating raw materials, polymers, inorganic materials)
- Rubber chemicals and sealing materials
- Machinery and equipment, precision parts
- Electronic components and modules
- Medical devices and lab consumables
- Feed additives and bio-based products
- Consumer goods, home and textile brands
- Traders and distributors of industrial raw materials and consumer goods
- Niche specialists with a strong global share but little name recognition

Target markets: North America, Europe, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and South America.
Typical contacts: export or international sales director, head of international marketing, brand or marketing lead, owner or founder.

## 10. Quality and compliance

Lead Engine publicly commits to four red lines, written into the contract:

1. **No fabricated data**: any technical specification the client has not provided in writing never appears in deliverables. A breach means the entire batch is redone at no charge.
2. **No ranking guarantees**: the commitment is to the quality of citable assets and a verifiable change in mention rate.
3. **No black-hat tactics**: no hidden text, no cloaking, no bulk link buying.
4. **Fully traceable data**: every test record has screenshots and timestamps, every published piece keeps a version history, and everything is handed over in full when the engagement ends. No technical lock-in.

Before publication, content passes four checkpoints: source verification (each delivery includes a source map listing every data point with its source file and page number), compliant competitor mapping, originality and structure check, and technical QA.
Full standard: https://ileadengineai.com/quality.html

Data and privacy: outbound contacts are cross-verified and every email address is verified at SMTP level before sending; GEO is built only on the client's real, verifiable specifications, certifications and supply capability, with no mass-distributed press releases or fabricated content. Personal data handling and GDPR rights are set out at https://ileadengineai.com/privacy.html
